problems: Repair pass on house-of-bourbon (5 findings plus the thin Beaujolais/Dombes item) and county-of-bearn (3 findings plus 2 thin items), 11 fixes applied; both re-validated with python3 -I tools/validate_dossier.py --resolve: house-of-bourbon 0 errors and 6 warnings (the place 'Vendôme' is not in the gazetteer), county-of-bearn 0 errors and 0 warnings. Dossiers comtat-venaissin, house-of-valois-anjou and huguenots were not touched.

house-of-bourbon now follows one rule (the ducal domain): La Marche is lost in 1341 (James I, younger son of Louis I) and gained in 1488 (Peter II becomes duke); Vendome is gained in May 1527; 1523-1526 holds no land and has no keyframe or capital. The Cliopatria shapes of 1375-1407 carry no Ain cell and no Rhone cell north of 46.02 N, so the Beaujolais and Dombes of 1400/1402 are stand-in regions added to every shape 1400-1522.

county-of-bearn and house-of-bourbon /ledger 1555-05 carry the identical region spec and text (Béarn proper by radius, the Cliopatria 1450 polygon, all Hautes-Pyrénées); Bigorre is outside Béarn 1390-1406 (Gaston III page: life annuity 5 January 1390; Bigorre page: sold by Bernard VII of Armagnac in 1407). The Bigorre page says Brétigny 1360 'made it decisively French' while the Gaston III page compensates Fébus for the loss of Bigorre: the pages disagree on 1360-1379.

County-of-bearn drawn area is about 6,830 km2 (1347-1378), 12,650 km2 (1379-1389, 1407-1554) and 7,590 km2 (1390-1406) against Cliopatria's 3,806 km2 (factor 3.3 at most); acknowledged in the notes. The page budget of 1-2 pages was exceeded to answer the reviewer (Bigorre, Nébouzan, Catherine of Navarre, Kingdom of Navarre, Antoine of Navarre).

The Cliopatria County of Foix row (1236-1555) and the Kingdom of Navarre / Albret lands overlap county-of-bearn and house-of-bourbon 1555; the owners of county-of-foix (eu-10) must agree the 1555 split with house-of-bourbon /ledger 1555 (three gains).
